identity.title: ALMA Spectral Survey of an Eruptive Young Star, V883 Ori (ASSAY). I. What Triggered the Current Episode of Eruption?

paper_type_evidence.quote: An unbiased spectral survey of V883 Ori, an eruptive young star, was carried out with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) in Band 6.

evidence.quote: It has a bolometric luminosity of $\sim$220 L$_\odot$ (cite: Furlan2016) at a distance of 388 pc (cite: jelee19).
It has a bolometric luminosity of $\sim$220 L$_\odot$ (cite: Furlan2016) at a distance of 388 pc (cite: jelee19).

question.value: What triggered the current eruption of V883 Ori, as seen in the morphology and kinematics of molecular lines from the envelope and disk?

evidence.quote: Together, these features suggest that the current episode of eruption in V883 Ori may be triggered by the infall from the envelope to the outer disk
carried out in band 6 during Cycle 7 (2019.1.00377.S, PI: Jeong-Eun Lee)
The spectral survey covers from $\sim$221 to $\sim$275 GHz with three Science Goals (SGs)

analysis_steps.goal: Kinematics: PV diagrams and model velocity comparison

method.value: PV diagrams along the disk semi-major axis compared with Keplerian rotation; model moment 9 maps convolved to observed resolution

evidence.quote: All three PV diagrams follow well the Keplerian rotation velocity profile, with a central mass of 1.2 M$_\odot$.

assumptions.value: Distance 388 pc, M*=1.2 Msun, inclination 38.3 deg, PA ~120 deg

evidence.quote: The inclination inferred from the ratio between the disk semi-major and semi-minor axes is 38.3 $\pm$ 1 $^\circ$ (cite: cieza16)

validation.value: C17O consistent with the Keplerian model

evidence.quote: The C$^{17}$O moment 9 map, which is the best tracer of the Keplerian disk, is consistent with the model.

method.value: Fit HCN peak positions with logarithmic and Archimedean spirals; compute Q for current and pre-burst temperature

evidence.quote: the logarithmic spiral with $R=R_0 e^{a\theta}$, developed by the gravitational instability and the Archimedean spiral with $R=R_0 + b\theta$
If the snowline was located at 4 au, then $Q < 2$ at $r < 100$ au and $Q \sim 3.5$ at 200 au

validation.value: Southern arm well fit, northern not; shape ambiguous

evidence.quote: The northern arm does not reveal a spiral profile, while the southern arm is well-fit.
The calibration was performed using the CASA pipeline (6.2.1.7)
the continuum level is automatically measured using STATCONT

The outer boundary of the gas disk is at r$\sim$0.8$''$.
it is greater than 2 at all radii and $\sim$7 at 200 au

findings_qualitative.value: HDO, COMs, HDCO, HNCO and OCS emission is confined within the water sublimation radius, and HCO+ has a hole due to destruction by water

evidence.quote: Molecular emission from complex organic molecules (COMs) is confined within the HDO emission boundary, and HCO$^+$ has an emission hole

claims.hypothesis: The current eruption was triggered by infall from the envelope onto the outer disk
claims.experiment: Mapped many molecular lines and inspected morphology and kinematics
claims.result: Arm-like structures in HCO+ and SO, red-shifted absorption, tentative spirals in HCN and H2CO
claims.finding: Infall may have induced a spiral wave that propagated inward and triggered the burst

evidence.quote: the current episode of eruption in V883 Ori may be triggered by the infall from the envelope to the outer disk, generating a spiral wave

claims.hypothesis: HDO traces the water sublimation region, and COMs sublimate with it
claims.experiment: Moment maps of HDO and COMs
claims.result: HDO emission radius ~0.3''; COMs lie within it
claims.finding: COMs are co-located with water sublimation

evidence.quote: HDO was detected in the disk, demonstrating that COMs are sublimated along with water.

claims.hypothesis: Spiral structure is consistent with gravitational instability
claims.experiment: Toomre Q computed for current and pre-burst temperatures
claims.result: Q>2 now; Q<2 inside 100 au if the pre-burst snowline was at 4 au
claims.finding: Spirals could have developed before the burst; the disk is now stable

evidence.quote: Therefore, currently, the disk appears gravitationally stable.

why_this_method.value: Moments 8 and 9 are used where line blending or hyperfine structure contaminates moments 0 and 1

evidence.quote: moment 8 and 9 maps better present the distribution of the dominating line emission

limitations_admitted.value: Velocity resolution and S/N are too low to robustly examine arm kinematics and spirals

evidence.quote: the velocity resolution of our data is not high enough to robustly examine the kinematics of the large arm-like structures beyond the disk.

referee_caveats_inferred: Spiral and streamer features are tentative and qualitative
Trigger scenario is inferred, with no quantitative modelling
Pre-burst temperature assumption (snowline at 4 au) is unconstrained
Optically thick lines are partially filtered out in the absorption channel

missing_for_reproduction: Spiral fit and Q calculation details
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Large: 60 SPW cubes over 7 executions, probably several hundred GB to ~1 TB
reproducibility.score_reason: Calibration and weighting are given, but imaging parameters and the qualitative analysis are underspecified.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Results are mostly qualitative morphology with few numeric answer keys, and the imaging recipe is incomplete.
